newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Small Hong Kong share issues seen yielding gains.
newsitem.headline: Small Hong Kong share issues seen yielding gains.

text.p: Many of Hong Kong's recent IPOs have offered investors poor returns, but analysts said quick gains can be made in the coming weeks with a number of small, low-priced issues expected to attract retail investors.
Analysts said initial public offerings (IPOs) of smaller companies are expected to be priced at lower price earnings (PE) multiples of about six to seven times, to ensure a following.
"Short-term investors will choose some (IPOs) which have relatively low listing PEs," said Carol Lai, research manager at SOCGEN-Crosby Securities.
Some of Hong Kong's recent large issues, such as SmarTone Telecommunications Holdings Ltd and Anhui Expressway Co Ltd, rapidly saw their share prices fall below their IPO prices.
Anhui Expressway has a weighted average prospective PE multiple of 20.8 times, and SmarTone of 12.8 times.
But, smaller and cheaper IPOs, such as Arts Optical International Holdings Ltd and China Resources Beijing Land Ltd, surged on their market debuts earlier this month.
Shares of Arts Optical, whose IPO was 261 times subscribed, ended their debut at HK$2.25, compared with an issue price of HK$1.00. The firm's price earnings multiple was 5.88 times.
China Resources Beijing Land's IPO was 125.7 times subscribed in Hong Kong. Its shares ended their debut up 71.6 percent at HK$4.05. The company's prospective PE multiple was 9.3 times.

"PE and discount to NAV (net asset value) are deemed important. Major property developers are trading at about 15 times PE while mid-cap (property developers) are trading at about 10 times," said Lai.
Alex Tang, research director from Yamaichi International, said apart from price earnings ratios (PER), it was hard to obtain much information from listing documents.
"That leads to an impression that PER is a main criteria for investment considerations," he said.

The next new issue to be listed in Hong Kong is Citybus Group Ltd. The subscription period for the bus operator's IPO closed on Friday and the 250 million share offering, at HK$1.42 a share, is expected to be about 50 times subscribed, analysts said.
Citybus has a PE multiple of 11.5 times. Dealing in the shares is expected to begin on November 29.

Data storage products maker Jackin International Holdings Ltd began a public offering of 97 million shares last week at HK$1.05 a share and is expected to be listed by the end of this month. It has a PE multiple of 5.0 times.

Starting on November 19, RNA Holdings Ltd, a demerged metal operation of bullion, jewellery and property concern Tem Fat Hing Fung (Holdings) Ltd, is expected to kick off a HK$170 million IPO at HK$1.01 per share.

Another upcoming small issue is Nam Fong International Holdings Ltd. The China property concern is expected to price its shares at a prospective PE multiple of 6.7 to 8.1 times, giving a 30 percent to 40 percent discount to NAV. The subscription period for its IPO is expected to run from November 26 to 29.
Nam Fong is expected to issue 340 million shares, of which 68 million will be offered in Hong Kong, at a price ranging from HK$2.50 to HK$3.00 per share.
Analysts said once the shares begin trading, investors turn to fundamentals for further share price direction.
"The fundamentals will dictate the stock price performance afterwards," said Lai.

Meanwhile, local retail investors are expected to give APT Satellite Holdings Ltd a rather cool reception due to its larger issue size and the disappointing performance of its counterpart Asia Satellite Telecommunications Holdings Ltd
APT plans to raise US$250 million through a dual listing in Hong Kong and New York and the share offering is expected to attract mainly professional investors, analysts said.
